The Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development has received over $20 million in Specialty Crop Block Grant funding since the program began. Patients often sought ways to integrate their new roles as sick parents into their existing identities, finding that healthcare professionals played a critical role in this process. Another theme was the balancing act patients engaged in when communicating with healthcare professionals about their children. On one hand, patients wanted to ensure that their children received adequate care and support, which often required them to be open and honest with healthcare providers about their family situation. On the other hand, patients also felt the need to protect their children from the full extent of their illness, which sometimes led to selective disclosure or even avoidance of certain topics. The study also highlighted the importance of patient-centered care in this context. Healthcare professionals who took the time to listen to patients' concerns about their children and provided tailored advice and resources were seen as particularly helpful. Patients appreciated when healthcare providers offered guidance on how to explain the illness to children, how to manage practical issues such as school and childcare, and how to support children's emotional needs during and after treatment. In conclusion, this qualitative study underscores the complex and often disruptive nature of cancer patients' biographies when they have dependent children. texts.full_text: [A case of primary adenocarcinoma of the epididymis]. A 68-year-old man presented with right intrascrotal swelling. On palpation, a hard tumor without pain was recognized at the head of the right epididymis. Power Doppler ultrasonography revealed blood flow signals within the tumor. Surgical exploration was performed under the tentative diagnosis as possible malicious transformation (carcinoma in situ) or an invasive adenocarcinoma based on clinical suspicion and imaging findings. A partial orchiopexy with wide local excision of the epididymis confirmed a primary adenocarcinoma, diagnosed at histopathological examination confirming non-invasive carcinoma cells within glandular lumens without lymphovascular invasion nor perineural or capsular extension detected during surgery further assessment by an urologic oncologist led to recommendations for additional management including radiation therapy as adjuvant treatment and regular follow-ups with imaging studies due to the potential risk of systemic spread if not curatively resected. The patient was counseled about options, risks associated with different treatments available like conservative (watchful waiting), local excision alone or radical surgery which includes both lymphadenectomy plus possibly retroperitoneal testis removal given their role as a possible site for occult metastasis based on his clinical scenario and the stage at presentation of this primary tumor. The patient opted for aggressive surgical intervention to prevent any potential delay in detection leading into potentially worse prognosis due largely being asymptomatic without signs indicating regional spread or systemic involvement, thus he chose immediate treatment instead avoiding further escalating risk through surveillance-based strategy waiting until symptoms progressed This case underscores the importance of maintaining high clinical suspicion regarding uncommon primary tumors originating within epididymis and also highlights how early intervention with adequate surgery can alter outcomes dramatically positively compared against delayed diagnosis where progression may be inevitable despite subsequent treatments being undertaken thereafter
